source.note: 英文逐字稿取自 YouTube 字幕；中文為學習用翻譯。版權屬原作者，僅供個人學習。

title: The Best Professional Connectors to Explain Your Opinions in English

lines.en: How many times have you shared an opinion in English, but halfway through your words weren't really coming together as smoothly as you wanted?
lines.zh: 你有多少次用英文分享意見，講到一半卻發現話說得不如預期順暢？

lines.en: Maybe you found yourself saying too much or searching for the right words, trying to wrap up your thoughts.
lines.zh: 也許你發現自己講太多，或一直在找對的字，想把想法收尾。

lines.en: This might happen, for example, when a coworker asks for your opinion in a meeting and again,
lines.zh: 舉例來說，這可能發生在同事在會議上問你的意見，

lines.en: you have a difficult time explaining why you have a certain perspective or perhaps a friend shares her thoughts about a movie you just saw.
lines.zh: 而你很難解釋自己為什麼有某個觀點；或是朋友分享她對你們剛看完的電影有什麼想法時。

lines.en: And again, you're not really sure how to put your ideas into place.
lines.zh: 同樣地，你不太確定要怎麼把想法組織好。

lines.en: If that sounds familiar to you, here's what I want you to know.
lines.zh: 如果這聽起來很熟悉，我想讓你知道一件事。

lines.en: It's not at all because your English isn't good enough.
lines.zh: 這完全不是因為你的英文不夠好。

lines.en: It's simply because you don't have the right connectors in place: words like because, so that, and due to.
lines.zh: 只是因為你沒有準備好對的連接詞：像是 because、so that 和 due to 這些字。

lines.en: These connectors improve your flow and help your ideas to feel structured rather than scattered.
lines.zh: 這些連接詞能讓你說話更流暢，讓你的想法有條理，而不是零散。

lines.en: They also help you explain your reasoning, which makes your opinion stronger and more engaging.
lines.zh: 它們也能幫你解釋理由，讓你的意見更有力、更吸引人。

lines.en: Ultimately, this helps you sound confident and professional.
lines.zh: 最終，這會讓你聽起來有自信又專業。

lines.en: Instead of sounding hesitant or unsure of your own opinions.
lines.zh: 而不是對自己的意見猶豫不決、沒把握。

lines.en: I want you to think about it for a moment.
lines.zh: 我希望你想一想。

lines.en: When you hear someone confidently explain why they believe something, doesn't it make their opinion more persuasive?
lines.zh: 當你聽到有人很有自信地解釋他為什麼相信某件事，是不是讓他的意見更有說服力？

lines.en: That's exactly what we're going to work on today.
lines.zh: 這正是我們今天要練習的。

lines.en: By the end of this lesson, you'll have the best professional connectors to explain your reasoning smoothly.
lines.zh: 上完這一課，你會學到最好的專業連接詞，能流暢地解釋你的理由。

lines.en: You'll also have a simple structure to make your opinions sound polished and professional in English.
lines.zh: 你也會有一個簡單的架構，讓你的英文意見聽起來精練又專業。

lines.en: Ultimately, you'll have more confidence in sharing your thoughts without hesitation or over-explaining.
lines.zh: 最終，你會更有自信分享想法，不會猶豫也不會解釋過頭。

lines.en: Now, I want you to stick with me because at the end I do have a challenge for you so you can put all of these strategies together and start using the right connectors to get started.
lines.zh: 我希望你一直看到最後，因為最後我有一個挑戰給你，讓你把這些策略全部結合起來，開始使用對的連接詞。

lines.en: Let's talk about how to structure your opinion so that it's clear, logical, and easy to follow.
lines.zh: 我們來談談如何組織你的意見，讓它清楚、有邏輯、容易理解。

lines.en: English speakers naturally use a three part structure when we're expressing an opinion.
lines.zh: 英語母語者表達意見時，自然會用一種三段式架構。

lines.en: The first step is to clearly state your opinion.
lines.zh: 第一步是清楚說出你的意見。

lines.en: This is where you introduce your perspective in a direct confident way.
lines.zh: 這是你用直接、有自信的方式提出觀點的地方。

lines.en: Most of the time, you're going to hear this with a sentence starter like I believe, I think, I would say, and I feel, followed by that immediate statement of your perspective.
lines.zh: 大多數時候，你會聽到它以 I believe、I think、I would say、I feel 這類句子開頭，後面緊接著說出你的觀點。

lines.en: Step two is to explain why, and this is where the connectors come in.
lines.zh: 第二步是解釋原因，這就是連接詞派上用場的地方。

lines.en: Strong opinions should be supported by clear reasoning and connectors help you explain the why behind your statement.
lines.zh: 有力的意見應該有清楚的理由支持，而連接詞能幫你解釋說法背後的原因。

lines.en: So again, this would include words such as because, since, and due to. However, we're going to learn many more in this lesson today.
lines.zh: 所以這會包括 because、since 和 due to 這些字。不過今天這一課我們會學到更多。

lines.en: Before we get there, let's talk about the third step in a clear, logical opinion.
lines.zh: 在那之前，我們先來談清楚、有邏輯的意見的第三步。

lines.en: Wrap it up with a conclusion or a question.
lines.zh: 用結論或問題來收尾。

lines.en: Doing this makes your opinion feel complete or finished.
lines.zh: 這樣做會讓你的意見感覺完整、有結尾。

lines.en: You can do this by reinforcing your point or inviting further discussion.
lines.zh: 你可以強調你的論點，或邀請對方進一步討論。

lines.en: For example, after stating your opinion and why you have it, you might say, that's why I think this is a good solution, or what do you think?
lines.zh: 例如，在說出意見和理由之後，你可以說：這就是為什麼我覺得這是個好辦法；或是：你覺得呢？

lines.en: Before we get into our professional connectors, I want to give you two examples of this step-by-step process in action.
lines.zh: 在進入專業連接詞之前，我想給你兩個實際運用這個步驟的例子。

lines.en: We're gonna look at a social example and a professional, so let's imagine in a social setting I might say,
lines.zh: 我們會看一個社交場合的例子和一個職場的例子。假設在社交場合，我可能會說：

lines.en: I think the new wicked movie was great because the actors did justice to the roles and didn't stray from the original characters.
lines.zh: 我覺得新的《魔法壞女巫》電影很棒，因為演員把角色詮釋得很到位，沒有偏離原本的角色。

lines.en: What did you think about it?
lines.zh: 你覺得呢？

lines.en: I have my opinion, my reasoning, and a way to reinforce or invite discussion on that opinion.
lines.zh: 我有我的意見、我的理由，還有一個強化意見或邀請討論的方式。

lines.en: And now let's look at a professional option.
lines.zh: 現在來看職場的版本。

lines.en: I believe we should adjust the project timeline since the current deadlines don't give us enough time for quality control.
lines.zh: 我認為我們應該調整專案時程，因為目前的截止期限沒有給我們足夠的時間做品質管理。

lines.en: What's your take on this?
lines.zh: 你對這個有什麼看法？

lines.en: When you structure your opinion in English using this three-step process and when you include your reason why you have that particular opinion, your ideas are more clear and more persuasive.
lines.zh: 當你用這個三步驟架構組織英文意見，並加上你有這個意見的理由，你的想法會更清楚、更有說服力。

lines.en: Now of course, simply following this structure isn't enough.
lines.zh: 當然，光是照這個架構還不夠。

lines.en: The connectors you choose are going to determine how natural and confident you sound.
lines.zh: 你選用的連接詞，會決定你聽起來有多自然、多有自信。

lines.en: So let's go deeper into the best professional connectors you can use to explain your opinions clearly in English.
lines.zh: 所以我們更深入來看，有哪些最好的專業連接詞能幫你用英文清楚表達意見。

lines.en: We're going to explore three categories of connectors today and we'll start with the most important explaining why you think something or what happened as a result.
lines.zh: 今天我們會探討三類連接詞，先從最重要的開始：解釋你為什麼這樣想，或因此發生了什麼事。

lines.en: We need this because when you're expressing your opinion, you're not just saying what you think, you're answering an important question why, and this is where our connectors come in.
lines.zh: 我們需要它，是因為當你表達意見時，你不只是在說你怎麼想，你也在回答一個重要的問題：為什麼？這就是連接詞登場的地方。

lines.en: So let's start with cause or the reason why you have a particular belief or opinion.
lines.zh: 所以我們先從「原因」開始，也就是你有某個信念或意見的理由。

lines.en: In English we have several go-to words for this.
lines.zh: 英文有幾個常用的字可以表達這個。

lines.en: The first is the most common because which means for this reason.
lines.zh: 第一個是最常見的 because，意思是「因為這個理由」。

lines.en: Next on this list is since, and we use this when the reason for an opinion is already pretty clear or obvious.
lines.zh: 清單上的下一個是 since，當意見的理由已經很清楚或很明顯時使用。

lines.en: Now, similar to the word because, we can also use due to. It's very similar in meaning but slightly more formal.
lines.zh: 和 because 類似，我們也可以用 due to，意思非常接近，但稍微正式一點。

lines.en: And here's one more that has a very similar meaning: just like due to, we can use because of. These two function in the same way grammatically. However, of these two, due to is more formal, and because of is used more often in everyday conversation.
lines.zh: 還有一個意思非常相近的：跟 due to 一樣，我們可以用 because of。這兩個在文法上的用法相同，不過兩者之中，due to 比較正式，because of 比較常用在日常對話中。

lines.en: Now I've got one more in this list, but before I go there, I know you might be thinking Annemarie, it sounds like you've just given me a list of words that all have very similar meaning.
lines.zh: 清單上我還有一個，但在那之前，我知道你可能在想：Annemarie，你好像只是給我一串意思都很像的字。

lines.en: And you're right, English speakers love variety.
lines.zh: 你說得沒錯，英語母語者很愛變化。

lines.en: We like to use different vocabulary and sentence structures.
lines.zh: 我們喜歡用不同的字彙和句型。

lines.en: This allows us to have more than one way to express what we think.
lines.zh: 這讓我們能用不只一種方式表達想法。

lines.en: Now you don't have to start using all of these today.
lines.zh: 你不需要今天就開始全部用上。

lines.en: My recommendation is learn one or two connectors that are new to you.
lines.zh: 我的建議是，先學一兩個對你來說新的連接詞。

lines.en: Start incorporating them into your conversations and your writing and then once you're comfortable you can add a couple more.
lines.zh: 開始把它們融入你的對話和寫作中，熟練之後再加一兩個。

lines.en: Now, the last one on this particular list is the word as. Let's take a look at how these work.
lines.zh: 這張清單上的最後一個是 as。我們來看看這些字怎麼用。

lines.en: In real conversations, imagine you're talking about your company, the place where you work, and you might say, I like this company because the people are friendly.
lines.zh: 在實際對話中，想像你在談你的公司、你工作的地方，你可能會說：我喜歡這家公司，因為同事都很友善。

lines.en: Or maybe you're making weekend plans and you could say, since the sun is shining, let's go to the park.
lines.zh: 或是你在計畫週末，你可以說：既然出太陽了，我們去公園吧。

lines.en: Remember, we talked about using since to highlight that the reason for something is already clear and obvious.
lines.zh: 記得我們說過，用 since 來強調某件事的理由已經很清楚、很明顯。

lines.en: It is clear and obvious to everyone that the sun is shining and it's a good reason to go to the park.
lines.zh: 大家都看得出來出太陽了，這是去公園的好理由。

lines.en: If you needed to explain why you were late to a meeting, you might say I was late due to traffic.
lines.zh: 如果你需要解釋開會為什麼遲到，你可以說：我因為塞車遲到了。

lines.en: And when letting someone know why an event was canceled, you could say the meeting was canceled because of the storm.
lines.zh: 要告訴別人某個活動為什麼取消，你可以說：會議因為暴風雨取消了。

lines.en: And here's one more using as: As our local coffee shop has closed, we have to drive two miles away for good coffee.
lines.zh: 再一個用 as 的例子：因為我們附近的咖啡店關了，我們得開兩英里去喝好咖啡。

lines.en: Before we move on to our next category, I want to talk about something that is grammatically important when we're using the words due to and because of. These are always followed by a noun, like traffic,
lines.zh: 在進入下一類之前，我想談一件文法上很重要的事：使用 due to 和 because of 時，後面一定要接名詞，像是 traffic、

lines.en: the storm, or the delay. For example, I cannot say I was late due to it was raining.
lines.zh: the storm 或 the delay。例如，我不能說 I was late due to it was raining。

lines.en: That doesn't work for us.
lines.zh: 這樣說是不對的。

lines.en: Instead you would say, I was late because it was raining.
lines.zh: 你應該說：I was late because it was raining。

lines.en: This is a simple but important difference.
lines.zh: 這是簡單但很重要的差別。

lines.en: Now, at the start of this section, I highlighted that we're looking at words that help us explain why or what happened,
lines.zh: 在這一段開頭，我特別提到我們要看能幫我們解釋「為什麼」或「發生了什麼」的字，

lines.en: so let's take a look at a few more connectors that help us express the what happened, what was the result of something.
lines.zh: 所以我們再來看幾個能表達「發生了什麼」、某件事結果如何的連接詞。

lines.en: For that we use words like so, and this helps us to show a consequence or an outcome.
lines.zh: 這時我們用 so 這類的字，它能幫我們表示後果或結果。

lines.en: We might also use which is why.
lines.zh: 我們也可以用 which is why。

lines.en: This explains a reason at the end of a sentence.
lines.zh: 它用在句子後半，說明理由帶來的結果。

lines.en: Let's take a look at a few examples.
lines.zh: 我們來看幾個例子。

lines.en: Let's say that you studied really hard for some exams and you want to highlight the result.
lines.zh: 假設你為了考試非常用功讀書，你想強調結果。

lines.en: You might say, I studied hard so I passed all three exams.
lines.zh: 你可以說：我很用功，所以三科考試都過了。

lines.en: Or maybe your team just had a really successful meeting and in telling someone else about it, you might say the meeting went well, which is why we got the project.
lines.zh: 或者你的團隊剛開了一場很成功的會議，跟別人說的時候，你可以說：會議很順利，所以我們拿到了那個專案。

lines.en: Now, before we move on to our second category of connectors, I want to give you a challenge to practice.
lines.zh: 在進入第二類連接詞之前，我想給你一個練習挑戰。

lines.en: I want you to think about something that you did recently.
lines.zh: 想想你最近做過的一件事。

lines.en: Maybe you just started to learn English, maybe you changed jobs or maybe you moved to a new city.
lines.zh: 也許你剛開始學英文，也許你換了工作，也許你搬到新的城市。

lines.en: How would you explain why?
lines.zh: 你會怎麼解釋原因？

lines.en: For example, you might start with: I started learning English because..., or: Since I wanted to improve my communication skills, I..., or: Due to my work environment, I decided... Take a moment to finish those example sentences.
lines.zh: 例如，你可以用這些開頭：I started learning English because...，或 Since I wanted to improve my communication skills, I...，或 Due to my work environment, I decided...。花點時間把這些例句完成。

lines.en: As always, you can also share them with me in the comments below.
lines.zh: 一樣，你也可以在下方留言分享給我。

lines.en: Now that we've covered connectors for cause and result, let's move on to purpose.
lines.zh: 我們已經學了表達原因和結果的連接詞，接下來看「目的」。

lines.en: To further explain the why behind your decisions.
lines.zh: 用來進一步解釋你做決定背後的原因。

lines.en: Just like expressing what you think.
lines.zh: 就像表達你的想法一樣。

lines.en: When you share a thought or a decision that you've already made, you're not just talking about what you did, you might also need to explain why you did it.
lines.zh: 當你分享一個想法或已經做的決定時，你不只是在講你做了什麼，你可能也需要解釋為什麼這樣做。

lines.en: And for that we use purpose connectors.
lines.zh: 這時我們就用表達目的的連接詞。

lines.en: I want to share with you three great ways to express why you did something.
lines.zh: 我想和你分享三個表達為什麼做某件事的好方法。

lines.en: The first is in order to, this is more formal and allows you to emphasize your intention.
lines.zh: 第一個是 in order to，比較正式，能讓你強調你的意圖。

lines.en: Now a more informal everyday conversational version of in order to is simply using the word to, and I'll share an example with you in a moment.
lines.zh: 比較非正式、日常對話中的 in order to，就是只用 to 這個字，我等一下會給你例子。

lines.en: The third in this category is so that, and this focuses on the ultimate desired response.
lines.zh: 這一類的第三個是 so that，它著重在最終想要的結果。

lines.en: Here's what all of these would sound like in real conversational examples.
lines.zh: 這些用在實際對話中會是這樣。

lines.en: Let's start with evaluating why you started to learn English for work.
lines.zh: 我們先來看你為什麼開始為了工作學英文。

lines.en: You might say, I'm taking these lessons in order to communicate better at work.
lines.zh: 你可以說：我上這些課是為了在工作上溝通得更好。

lines.en: Again, using in order to is a more formal version.
lines.zh: 再說一次，用 in order to 是比較正式的說法。

lines.en: You might also say, I joined this course to improve my speaking skills, or I'm studying English so that I can work abroad.
lines.zh: 你也可以說：我參加這個課程是為了提升口說能力；或是：我學英文，這樣我就能去國外工作。

lines.en: Again, in that example, we're emphasizing the ultimate goal or desire that you have.
lines.zh: 同樣地，在這個例子中，我們強調的是你最終的目標或願望。

lines.en: Now, I want to pause here for a moment, because in category one, focusing on cause and result, we had so as a connector, and here, when talking about purpose, we had so that. What's the difference?
lines.zh: 我想在這裡停一下，因為在第一類，也就是原因和結果中，我們有 so 這個連接詞，而這裡講目的時，我們有 so that。差別在哪裡？

lines.en: Let's take a look at two example sentences to help.
lines.zh: 我們來看兩個例句。

lines.en: The first is: I went by car so that I could take more luggage to the hotel. With so that, we're highlighting the purpose for making that decision.
lines.zh: 第一個是：我開車去，這樣就能帶更多行李到飯店。用 so that，我們強調的是做這個決定的目的。

lines.en: What pros and cons did we evaluate in order to come to that decision?
lines.zh: 我們評估了哪些優缺點，才做出這個決定？

lines.en: We could also say, I went by car so I was able to take more luggage to the hotel.
lines.zh: 我們也可以說：我開車去，所以能帶更多行李到飯店。

lines.en: Here we're emphasizing the ultimate result.
lines.zh: 這裡我們強調的是最後的結果。

lines.en: It might not have been a factor in the original decision, but it was a positive result.
lines.zh: 它可能不是最初做決定時考慮的因素，但卻是一個好的結果。

lines.en: In the end, one is about what you intended to do and the other is about what happened in the end.
lines.zh: 說到底，一個是你打算做什麼，另一個是最後發生了什麼。

lines.en: So now let's do a quick practice again.
lines.zh: 那我們再做一次快速練習。

lines.en: I want you to think about a decision that you've made recently.
lines.zh: 想想你最近做的一個決定。

lines.en: Maybe you changed jobs or signed up for a new English class.
lines.zh: 也許你換了工作，或報名了新的英文課。

lines.en: I want you to try finishing these sentences.
lines.zh: 試著完成這些句子。

lines.en: I started learning English to..., or I changed careers so that... And now, what if you need to give more than one reason for your opinion?
lines.zh: I started learning English to...，或 I changed careers so that...。那如果你需要給出不只一個理由來支持意見呢？

lines.en: That's where our next category of connectors comes in because sometimes one reason isn't enough.
lines.zh: 這就是下一類連接詞登場的地方，因為有時候一個理由不夠。

lines.en: Maybe you love your neighborhood where you live and there are multiple reasons why.
lines.zh: 也許你很愛你住的社區，原因不只一個。

lines.en: Or maybe you think a decision at work is a great idea, but there's more than one benefit that you want to highlight.
lines.zh: 或者你覺得公司的某個決定很棒，但你想強調的好處不只一個。

lines.en: For clear organized speech, we use connectors to add more details and here's how we can do that.
lines.zh: 為了讓說話清楚有條理，我們用連接詞來補充更多細節，方法如下。

lines.en: The first is another reason is. This allows us to add a separate second reason to support a decision or an opinion. We can also use
lines.zh: 第一個是 another reason is，這讓我們能加上另一個獨立的理由，來支持一個決定或意見。我們也可以用

lines.en: plus. This is a bit more casual, quite often used in everyday speech. Similar to plus is also, very neutral and commonly used.
lines.zh: plus，這比較口語，很常用在日常對話中。和 plus 類似的是 also，語氣中性，也很常用。

lines.en: And a fourth option is on top of that.
lines.zh: 第四個選項是 on top of that。

lines.en: This adds emphasis and may be used to highlight a surprising detail.
lines.zh: 它能加強語氣，可以用來強調令人意外的細節。

lines.en: Now again, let's take a look at all of these in action.
lines.zh: 我們再來看看這些字實際怎麼用。

lines.en: Let's say that someone asks you, do you like your new neighborhood?
lines.zh: 假設有人問你：你喜歡你的新社區嗎？

lines.en: And you might say, I love my new neighborhood because it's so close to work.
lines.zh: 你可以說：我很愛我的新社區，因為離公司很近。

lines.en: On top of that my friends live there and there are many great restaurants nearby.
lines.zh: 除此之外，我的朋友住在那裡，附近還有很多很棒的餐廳。

lines.en: Or imagine you're trying to explain why you support a particular company policy.
lines.zh: 或想像你在解釋為什麼支持公司某項政策。

lines.en: You might say this new work from home policy is great for those who prefer to work at different times of the day.
lines.zh: 你可以說：這項新的居家工作政策，對喜歡在一天中不同時段工作的人來說很棒。

lines.en: Also, it helps employees save money on commuting. And here's one more.
lines.zh: 而且，它還能幫員工省下通勤的錢。再一個例子。

lines.en: Let's say that you're giving feedback to someone on a new cafe that you tried.
lines.zh: 假設你在給一家剛去過的新咖啡廳意見。

lines.en: You might say, I love this new cafe, the coffee's excellent, plus they have delicious pastries.
lines.zh: 你可以說：我很愛這家新咖啡廳，咖啡很棒，而且他們的糕點也很好吃。

lines.en: Now, one important thing to keep in mind about using on top of that or another reason is both of these can only be used at the beginning of a sentence.
lines.zh: 使用 on top of that 或 another reason is 時，有一件重要的事要記住：兩者都只能放在句首。

lines.en: And once again, let's do a bit of practice.
lines.zh: 我們再來練習一下。

lines.en: I want you to think of something that you really enjoy or support.
lines.zh: 想一件你真的很喜歡或支持的事。

lines.en: It could be your job, a new hobby, a policy change, or even a favorite restaurant.
lines.zh: 可以是你的工作、新嗜好、政策改變，甚至是最喜歡的餐廳。

lines.en: How would you give two reasons for your particular opinion? You could try.
lines.zh: 你會怎麼用兩個理由支持你的意見？你可以試試看。

lines.en: I love... because... plus...; or: One reason I support... is..., another reason is... And now let's do a quick recap.
lines.zh: I love... because... plus...；或 One reason I support... is..., another reason is...。現在來快速複習一下。

lines.en: Today we did quite a few things.
lines.zh: 今天我們做了不少事。

lines.en: We started with a three step structure to ensure that you can share a clear, well organized opinion in English.
lines.zh: 我們先學了三步驟架構，確保你能用英文分享清楚、有條理的意見。

lines.en: Then we learned a variety of connectors for cause and result explaining why something happened.
lines.zh: 接著學了各種表達原因和結果的連接詞，解釋某件事為什麼發生。

lines.en: Next, we moved on to purpose connectors showing why you did something, and finally we learned how to add extra reasons to strengthen an opinion.
lines.zh: 然後我們學了目的連接詞，說明你為什麼做某件事，最後學了如何補充更多理由來強化意見。

lines.en: So now I want you to put all of this into practice.
lines.zh: 現在我希望你把這些全部付諸練習。

lines.en: Here's my challenge for you.
lines.zh: 這是我給你的挑戰。

lines.en: I want you to think about this question.
lines.zh: 請你想想這個問題。

lines.en: Why did you choose to learn English?
lines.zh: 你為什麼選擇學英文？

lines.en: In your answer, I want you to try to use at least two connectors from today's lesson.
lines.zh: 回答時，試著至少用上今天學到的兩個連接詞。

lines.en: You might begin with: I started learning English because..., or since I wanted to improve my communication skills, or I'm learning English
lines.zh: 你可以這樣開頭：I started learning English because...，或 since I wanted to improve my communication skills，或 I'm learning English

lines.en: so that..., and another reason is... As always, you can share your answers and your questions with me in the comments below.
lines.zh: so that...，還有 another reason is...。一樣，你可以在下方留言分享你的答案和問題。

lines.en: Also, if you found this lesson helpful to you, I would love to know, give this lesson a thumbs up here on YouTube and while you're at it, make sure you subscribe so you never miss one of my Confident English lessons.
lines.zh: 另外，如果你覺得這堂課有幫助，我很想知道，請在 YouTube 上按個讚，順便訂閱，就不會錯過任何一堂 Confident English 課程。

lines.en: Thank you so much for joining me and I look forward to seeing you next time.
lines.zh: 非常感謝你的參與，期待下次再見。
